subject: Transportation Systems
title: Dealing with Water
description: A short lesson to help you apply Dealing with Water.

hook.text: Dig below any city and you'll hit water. Subway builders spend as much time pumping as digging.

buildup.text: Groundwater seeps through cracks, floods shafts, and softens the soil tunnels pass through.

discovery.text: Engineers freeze the ground, inject concrete, or lower the water table with dewatering wells.

twist.text: Even finished subways pump constantly. New York's subway removes 13 million gallons of water daily.

climax.text: If the pumps stopped, many subway tunnels would flood within 36 hours.

punchline.text: Every subway is a boat that forgot to float.

quiz.question: How much water does the New York subway pump out daily?
